description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Change timers that already exist: start, pause, reset, restart, log a flip, silence, or delete. Select them by name or id, or by state. To add or remove time use adjust_timer instead. To make a dish that has not started wait for another (the potatoes 30 minutes after the chicken goes in) use action `link` with `startsAfter`; `unlink` clears it. Starting the other dish early or late then moves the linked dish with it. kitchen_status shows each link as startsAfterTimerId / startsAfterWhen / startsAfterMinutes.

action.description: start — run an idle timer or resume a paused one. pause — freeze a running timer, keeping the time left, and cancel its backup alarm. reset — back to idle at full duration, discarding the flip log; NOTE this abandons a live run WITHOUT recording it in history, matching the app. restart — run a finished timer again from the top. flip — log a manual flip on a running timer without changing the deadline. silence — stop the alarm ringing without changing the timer. delete — remove the timer entirely; unlike reset, an abandoned live run IS recorded in history as stopped early.

notify.description: Buzz the phone about this change. Default false — the cook usually asked for it out loud.

scope.description: Act on every timer in this state instead of naming them. scope 'idle' with action 'start' is the app's 'Start all' button. Give this or 'timers', not both.

startsAfter.description: Only with action `link`: the dish to follow. The linked timer must be idle or waiting (not started), and the other timer may not itself wait on it.

minutes.description: Minutes after that moment. 0 or left out: right then.

timer.description: The other timer's id or label from kitchen_status.

when.description: Count from when the other timer starts, or from when it finishes.

timers.description: Timer ids or labels from kitchen_status. Case-insensitive; an ambiguous label is an error listing the candidates. Give this or 'scope', not both.

name: control_timers

applied.description: What changed, with the state before and after.

delivery.description: How recently the phone checked in, so you never imply it has seen this.

lastSyncAgo.description: Last sync in words, e.g. '2m ago'.

notified.description: A push about this change went out.

phoneAlert.description: Whether the paired device's backup alarm armed, and which device that is. armed:false is a real answer, not an error.

alarmsArmed.description: Finish alarms armed by this call.

armed.description: true only if a server alarm is set AND this phone can receive push.

device.description: Which device will ring: the phone app (Android or installed app), a browser tab (rings only while the tab stays open), no paired device, or one that has not said (older version).

pushedToPhone.description: A notification about this change was sent.

reason.description: Why nothing armed, in words worth repeating to the cook.

startRemindersArmed.description: Start reminders armed for scheduled dishes.

summary.description: One sentence naming the device that will ring, worth repeating to the cook as is.

willAlertWhileAsleep.description: true only when armed AND the device is the phone app. A browser tab or an unknown device is never promised.

skipped.description: Matched timers the action did not apply to, and why.

warnings.description: Things worth saying out loud that are not failures.

title: Control timers
